Now P% = [(1.375x - x)/x] × 100

questions.question: By selling a watch for Rs. 1,600, a person gets profit that is equal to the loss of selling the same watch for Rs. 1,400. If the person wants to get a profit of 20%, at what price should he sell the watch?
questions.solution:

Profit earned by selling at Rs. 1600 is same as the loss incurred by selling the article for Rs. 1400

Formula:

Profit = SP – CP

Loss = CP – SP

Let the cost price of the article be Rs. x, then

1600 – x = x – 1400

⇒ x + x = 1600 + 1400

⇒ 2x = 3000

⇒ x = 1500

The cost price of the article is Rs.1500.

∴ The selling price of the article if it is sold at 20% profit = 1500 × (120/100) = Rs. 1800

**The answer is 1800.**

questions.question: The selling price of 84 items is equal to the cost price of 105 items. What is the percentage of profit gained in the transaction?

Selling price (SP) of 84 items = Cost price (CP) of 105 items

Percentage Profit = (Profit)/(Cost Price) times 100

Profit = SP - CP

Total Cost Price (CP) of 105 items = 105C

Total Selling Price (SP) of 84 items = 105C

Cost Price (CP) of 84 items = 84C

Profit = SP - CP

⇒ Profit = 105C - 84C

⇒ Profit = 21C

Percentage Profit = (Profit)/(Cost Price) times 100

⇒ Percentage Profit = (21C)/(84C) times 100

⇒ Percentage Profit = (21)/(84) times 100 

⇒ Percentage Profit = (1)/(4) times 100

⇒ Percentage Profit = 25%

**The percentage of profit gained in the transaction is 25%.**

questions.question: Ram bought a cell phone and paid 30% less than its original price. He sold it at 50% profit on the price he had paid. The percentage of profit earned by Ram on the original price was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Original Price = 100

Cost Price for Ram = 100 − 30% = 70

Selling Price = 70 + 50% of 70 = 105

Profit on Original Price = 105 − 100 = 5

Required Profit % = (5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount on Original Price = 30%

Profit on Cost Price = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = Original Price × (1 − Discount%)

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit%)

Profit % = [(SP − Original Price) ÷ Original Price] × 100

 
 Original Price
 100

 
 Cost Price

 Selling Price
 105

 Profit on Original Price = 5%

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the Original Price of the cell phone be 100.

⇒ Ram paid 30% less than the original price, so Cost Price (CP) = 100 − (30% of 100) = 70

⇒ He sold it at a 50% profit on his Cost Price.

⇒ Profit amount = 50% of 70 = 35

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 70 + 35 = 105

⇒ We need to find the profit percentage relative to the Original Price.

⇒ Profit earned on Original Price = SP − Original Price = 105 − 100 = 5

⇒ Percentage profit on Original Price = (5 ÷ 100) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is fundamentally always calculated on the Marked Price (or Original Price) unless stated otherwise. SP = MP × (1 − Discount%).

Successive Percentage Change

When a value undergoes two successive changes of a% and b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: [a + b + (a×b)÷100]%.

Base of Calculation

Usually, profit and loss are calculated over the Cost Price (CP). However, if specifically mentioned in the question (like in this case), it can be calculated over the Original Price or Marked Price.

questions.question: A man bought toffees at 3 for a rupee. How many toffees for a rupee must he sell to gain 50%?

P buys an article for Rs280 

Q at a profit of 25%

Profit = (S.P. - C.P.)

Profit% = ( Profit/ C.P.) × 100 

Where, S.P. = Selling Price , C.P. = Cost Price 

**CALCULATION:**

Here, Cost price of P = Rs280 , Profit% = 25%

S.P. of P = (100 + profit%)/100 × C.P.

Now, as P sells an article to Q 

So, S..P. of P = C.P. of Q = Rs350 

Now, according to the question 

R sells to S for Rs560 , Profit% = 40% 

S.P. = ( 100 + 40 ) /100 × C.P. 

⇒ 560 = 140/100 × C.P. 

⇒ C.P. = 560 × 100/140 = Rs400

questions.question: If 11 oranges are bought for Rs 10 and 10 oranges are sold for Rs 11, what is the profit or loss percentage?

Selling price of an orange = 11/10
